governors.mnote: Spent is the summary page's cumulative Total Expenditures, read from the text of each filed statement's summary report. Benson (committee 521875, formed 2025-01-22): $15,977,676.07; cumulative receipts $16,658,392.96 less that equals the filed ending balance $680,716.89 to the cent, and the six statements' opening and closing balances chain. James (John James for MI, 0606046) took public funding, so his statements carry separate primary and general election summaries, each with public and private funds: primary public $709,342.26 plus primary private $7,820,933.58 plus general private $3,329,695.70 (convention $0) is $11,859,971.54; his cycle receipts (private $12,402,854.30 plus public $709,342.26) less that equals the two ending cash balances ($35,467.11 primary plus $1,216,757.91 general) to the cent. Hudson (521876): cumulative $66,891.30; receipts $95,131.35 less that is $28.64 more than his filed ending balance ($28,211.41), the amount by which his July statement overlaps his pre-primary statement (2026-07-13 to 07-19). Brandenburg (520136): $0.00 cash spent in 2025-2026 on every statement; her $555,270.00 of in-kind contributions in 2026 are not counted (in-kind is left out everywhere), and her committee filed a dissolution statement. Michigan's expenditure totals include contributions refunded to donors, which are itemized as expenditures. Douglas Campbell's committee (0615274) has no campaign statement on file, so he is not collected. The earlier automated attempt was blocked; this was read in the browser.

Spent is the sum of Line 5 / Line 14 Total Expenditures on each filed report since 2025-01-01. Idaho's filed total includes in-kind expenditures (Little $14,030.44, Pickens $14,377.26, Stegner $7,420.65); subtract those for cash-only spending. Little's and Pickens's committees date from 2023, so their 2023-2024 annual reports are excluded; the results match each committee's cycle-to-date total on the September report minus the cycle-to-date total at the end of 2024 (Little $1,601,392.16 - $77,481.34; Pickens $166,727.31 - $12,591.13). Stegner registered 2026-01-29, and his cycle-to-date figure equals the total. Across all 33 period reports the three committees have filed (2023-2026), each report's beginning balance equals the prior ending balance. On each report, beginning balance plus contributions and loans minus expenditures equals the ending balance, and lines 8-13 sum to line 14, all to the cent. Itemized Schedule B entries (sum and count) match line 8 on all 29 reports counted.

The export carries itemized expenditures but no filed expenditure total, so spent is the sum of every itemized expenditure on the committees' reports (Shapiro for Pennsylvania, Garrity for PA). Completeness check: each report's filed beginning balance plus unitemized and itemized cash contributions plus other receipts minus itemized expenditures equals the next report's filed beginning balance to the cent, for all five report pairs from the 2025 annual through cycle 4, for both committees. The last report (cycle 5) cannot be balance-checked: its ending balance is not in the export and the state's report search site blocks scripted access. No amended reports were filed in the period. Garrity's own candidate filing shows one $2,000 contribution to her committee, excluded as a transfer. Ken Krawchuk (Libertarian) has no filer record in the 2025 or 2026 exports and is left out.

Summed 'Expenses Paid by Committee' from each filed report's summary totals (current versions). For both committees beginning balance + receipts - expenses = closing balance on every report, and each report opens at the prior report's close. Itemized disbursements in the SEEC 2026 election-year bulk file (updated 2026-10-31) match the filed totals to the cent for all 10 Lamont reports and 9 of 10 Fazio reports; Fazio's final weekly supplemental ($2,141,273.44, filed 2026-10-30) is not yet in the bulk file. Fazio includes $97.02 spent by his 2026 exploratory committee (2025-07-22 to 2025-08-27), excluding its $495.98 surplus transfer to the candidate committee. Fazio's campaign is publicly financed: $18,809,124.40 in Citizens' Election Program grants. Lamont is self-funded ($17,825,000 personal funds plus a $2,200,000 loan) and took no CEP grant.

Spent is the filed DR-2 Schedule B Expenditure Total summed over six reports per campaign: 2025 annual, Jan 1-May 14, May 15-May 26, May 27-Jul 14, Jul 15-Oct 14 and Oct 15-Oct 27 2026 (current filed versions, including amendments: Sand's 2025, May 27-Jul 14 and Jul 15-Oct 14 reports and Lahn's 2025 and Jan 1-May 14 reports were amended). On every report, cash on hand at start plus contributions, loans received and property sales minus expenditures and loan repayments equals cash on hand at end, to the cent, and each report's starting cash equals the prior report's ending cash. Itemized expenditures from the Board's searchable database, grouped by report period, equal each filed Schedule B total to the cent for both campaigns. Rob Sand for Iowa (committee 5185) existed before 2025; its 2024 report is excluded. Lahn for Governor (SWGA51409) started 2025 with $0; its $2,500,000 in outstanding loans are receipts, not spending.

Spent is the sum of each report's filed Total Disbursements (expenditures less adjustments for refunds). Gross expenditures before adjustments: Blackburn $12,504,452.18, Green $1,926,810.64, Hatley $9,052,277.65 (Hatley's gap is a $156,971.38 refund from Smoky Peak Advisors). Itemized expenditures sum to Total Expenditures on every report, except Blackburn's Q3 where the $364,847.52 difference equals that report's payments on obligations (checked). Beginning balance + receipts - disbursements = ending balance on every report, reports chain, and lifetime receipts - disbursements equals the final ending balance to the cent for all three. Blackburn counts only her state governor committee; her federal (FEC) committee is excluded. Pre-General report IDs: Blackburn 130121, Green 130397, Hatley 130506 (report pages need a search session, so no direct links).

Spent is the state's Total Expenditures for each candidate committee in the 2026 election cycle, from the Filing Entities list. Filed report PDFs need a login on this system, so each total was checked against the public itemized expenditure records instead. Friends of Cinde Warmington: $1,534,066.14; its 3,937 expenditure records across eight reports sum to that to the cent. Stephen Villee for New Hampshire: $2,952.57; its eight records sum to that to the cent. Kelly for New Hampshire (Ayotte): $8,835,703.83. Its records in the public feed sum to $8,228,944.13 (itemized $8,223,706.47 plus unitemized $5,237.66) across six of its seven reports; the report due 2026-09-02 (Aug 17 to 30, later amended) has no records in the feed, so the $606,759.70 difference could not be checked line by line. Her total includes $314,750.00 given to other registered committees. Spending by Ayotte's separate inaugural committee and her 2024 campaign is not counted. All spending here is monetary; none is in-kind. Read in the browser.

Itemized expenditures summed against filed cover-page totals; beginning balance plus contributions and other income minus expenditures equals ending balance for both campaigns, to the cent. Ramaswamy's itemized pre-general expenditures sum $3,939 above his filed total; the filed total is used.

Spent is TRACER's filed cycle-to-date Total Expenditures for each candidate committee (monetary; non-monetary expenditures excluded, as in the filed total). Itemized expenditure rows in the 2025 and 2026 bulk files, amendment offsets included, sum to each filed total to the cent for all three committees; Marx's 14 per-report monetary expenditure lines also sum to his total to the cent. Beginning balance $0 plus contributions and loans minus expenditures equals the ending balance to the cent for Weiser and Lopez. Marx's ending balance ($306,045.98) is $6,004.57 above $0 + contributions - expenditures; the gap is the net of mismatches between one report's ending cash and the next report's beginning cash (largest +$32,674.32 between the January and May 2026 reports), not an expenditure difference. Excluded: Weiser's prior attorney general committee and Lopez's 2022 governor committee.

Line 16 aggregate on each filed pre-general cover page matches the Guardian bulk expenditure extracts (2025 + 2026) summed by committee, to the cent. For Mazzei the extracts also include $1,564.07 of in-kind expenditures (line 17), which line 16 leaves out. The 2024 extract has no rows for any of the three committees. Period check (line 1 + line 8 - line 16 = line 21) and whole-life check (aggregate line 8 - aggregate line 16 = ending balance) both reconcile to the cent for all three. Munson's total includes $11,763.33 of officeholder expenses (line 14), and her receipts include $39,719.48 of surplus moved from her old House committee. Brooks's committee registered 2026-02-12 but reports one $11.40 expense dated 2025-12-31.

Spent is cash spending: line 9 (monetary expenses over $100) plus line 11 (expenses of $100 or less), using the 2026 Report 3 cumulative column plus the 2025 annual filing. In-kind expenses (line 10) are left out, as everywhere. Joe Lombardo: 2025 $900,249.22 + $1,119.45, 2026 $12,125,016.09 + $2,540.20, total $13,028,924.96. His 2026 opening balance $9,027,978.01 plus 2026 receipts ($5,877,073.69 over $100 and $52,013.13 of $100 or less) less 2026 spending equals the filed ending balance $2,829,508.54 to the cent; his 2025 filing's balance is $32,353.58 higher than its own receipts and spending explain. Reports filed for his Legal Defense Fund are not counted. Aaron Ford: 2025 $1,136,495.09 + $6,932.92 (his 2025 activity was filed under Governor; earlier years under Attorney General are not counted), 2026 $5,201,927.94 + $7,108.36, total $6,352,464.31. His filed fund balances do not reconcile with his own lines: the 2026 ending balance $1,374,168.89 is $89,381.06 higher than opening balance plus receipts less spending, and the 2025 one $21,659.04 higher; spending is taken as filed. Danielle Ford (on the ballot with no political party; her earlier filings were for school trustee and State Board of Education, her 2026 reports are filed under Governor): $1,820.00 in 2026, all in Report 3; receipts $2,600.00 less that equals her $780.00 ending balance. Read in the browser from each filed report's summary page.

Spent is the filed Total Expenditures on each report plus Total Amended Expenditure from amendments; in-kind items are excluded, as in the filed totals. Barlow: 2025 report $117,217.26 + primary $1,364,628.47 + primary amendment $16,731.52 + general $195,150.13. Bextel (committee Rebecca for Wyoming, formed for the general): general $12,369.40 + amendment filed 2026-10-29 $52,291.23. Her amendments filed 11/2 and 11/3 added contributions only. Carried-forward balances chain to the cent for both: Barlow starts at $0 for 2025 and ends at $319,871.13; Bextel starts at $0 and ends at $433,286.57. Itemized expenditure entries sum to every report's filed total to the cent. The state's PDFs print a row that crosses a page break twice; five such duplicate rows were removed before summing. Casner filed as a candidate with no committee, and both his primary report (from 2025-01-01) and his general report show $0 in contributions and expenditures.

Spent is the sum of current-version Cash Expenditure transactions in the ORESTAR export for each committee (Kotek 1,160; Drazan 1,964). Accounts payable (all marked satisfied and later paid in cash) and personal expenditures for reimbursement (repaid through cash expenditures) are left out so they are not counted twice; in-kind expenditures and contribution refunds are also left out. The full export's cash expenditures for 2025-01-01 onward equal the state's 2025 + 2026 Account Summary Cash Expenditures to the cent for both committees (Kotek $961,396.19 + $19,360,490.35; Drazan $315,639.34 + $21,619,420.96). On those summaries, beginning balance plus contributions and other receipts minus expenditures and other disbursements equals ending cash for both years, and the 2025 ending balance carries into 2026. No transaction dated on or before 2026-10-26 was filed after 2026-11-02. Excluded by the cutoff: transactions dated after 2026-10-26, which the account summaries above do include. In the export pulled 2026-11-04 these were Kotek $145,362.77 (all filed 2026-11-03) and Drazan $2,512,428.94 ($2,468,510.68 filed by 2026-11-02, $43,918.26 after), so each summary total less these equals the spent figure to the cent (Kotek $20,321,886.54 - $145,362.77 = $20,176,523.77; Drazan $21,935,060.30 - $2,512,428.94 = $19,422,631.36). Drazan's committee was registered for State Representative, 51st District, until 2025-10-27; $119,229.53 of her total was spent before that date. Kotek's committee is a continuing one that started 2025 with $891,062.45 on hand. Brett Smith (Pacific Green) is left out: his committee (Brett Smith for Change, ID 25051, registered 2026-06-04) has filed no transactions, and its account summary shows $0.

Spent is line 19 cash, total expenditures and disbursements: campaign expenditures, noncampaign disbursements and contributions to parties and other committees, in-kind excluded (Klobuchar $2,575,125.90, Demuth $19,899.45 in 2025 and $1,477,318.52 in 2026, Young $226.18). Minnesota's election-year reports are cumulative from January 1, so the pre-general report holds all 2026 spending. Read by eye from the filed PDFs and confirmed by arithmetic: on every report beginning balance plus line 10 cash receipts minus line 19 equals the filed ending balance to the cent, line 19 equals its parts, and Demuth's amended 2025 ending balance ($443,080.48) equals her 2026 beginning balance. Klobuchar's committee registered 2026-01-22 and Young's filed first in June 2026, so neither has a 2025 report. Demuth: 2025 $41,331.05 (amendment 3) plus 2026 $3,558,112.16. Demuth's receipts include a $1,293,702.93 public subsidy.

Spent is the filed D-2 Total Expenditures line summed over every quarterly report in the period (D2Totals.txt bulk file, filings listed in FiledDocs.txt; no amendments on file). That line includes transfers out to other committees: Pritzker $6,923,520.00, Bailey $6,550.00, Corbett $0; in-kind contributions are excluded. Beginning funds plus total receipts minus total expenditures equals ending funds on all 16 reports, to the cent, and each report's beginning funds equals the prior report's ending funds. Itemized expenditures (Expenditures.txt, part 8B) sum exactly to the filed itemized expenditure line on every report, and itemized transfers out (part 6B) sum exactly to the filed itemized transfers line. Committees: JB for Governor (ID 32762), Bailey for Illinois (34092; no spending in Q1-Q2 2025), Collin for Illinois (41172; formed 2026-05-01 with $5,000 opening funds, first report covers 2026-05-01 to 2026-06-30).

Spent is the sum of each report's filed 'Expenditures' line (in-kind expenditures and returned contributions excluded), primary and general campaigns combined. On every report the itemized expenditure details sum to the filed expenditure Total (expenditures + in-kind + returned) to the cent; starting balance + contributions + loans + account credits - expenditures - returned = ending balance; each report's starting balance equals the prior ending balance. Wilson files as 'Michael A. Wilson' (same filer record as his Attorney General campaigns since 2019); 8 reports. Johnson: 6 reports, using the amended versions of his initial and Q2 2026 reports. Michael Addison (United Citizens) is omitted: no campaign reports found for him.

Spent is the sum of each report's filed TOTAL of Expenses: Rhoden $70,593.75 + $914,052.53 + $2,760,044.38; Ahlers $8,706.76 + $155,697.56. SD reports expenses by category, not item by item; each report's categories sum to its filed operational total, and income lines sum to filed income. Beginning balance + income - expenses = ending balance on every report, to the cent, and each report opens at the prior report's closing balance. Rhoden's 2025 opening balance ($91,123.81) equals his 2024 year-end closing balance. Rhoden files scanned paper reports, read by eye. Amended versions were used (2025 year-end amended 2026-03-27, pre-general amended 2026-10-27); expense totals match the originals, and only contribution and donated-goods lines changed. Rhoden's pre-general total includes a $100,000 repayment of a loan from Larry and Sandy Rhoden that the committee received in the same period; without it, spending is $3,644,690.66. Both committees' totals include small contributions to party committees (Rhoden $3,680, Ahlers $300).

Spent is line 4, Total Expenditures and Other Disbursements, summed over the three reports, using Masterson's amended 2025 and pre-primary reports filed 2026-10-26 (the amendment raised his pre-primary expenditures from $1,023,845.63 to $1,024,428.53). Cash at beginning plus receipts minus expenditures equals cash at close on all six reports, to the cent, and each report's beginning cash equals the prior close. Itemized expenditures exported from the Secretary of State's statewide expenditure search, plus the filed unitemized ($50 or less) line, equal each filed total to the cent: Holscher 2025 $217,769.39 + $290.95, pre-primary $527,362.41 + $225.88, pre-general $2,328,537.66 + $0; Masterson 2025 $8,476.06 + $0, pre-primary $1,024,260.22 + $168.31, pre-general $1,714,982.54 + $966.83. Masterson's earlier reports are scanned images; their totals were read from the OCR text layer and confirmed by the balance and itemized checks.

Spent is the sum of line 8 Total Expenditures on each report. Sanders filed separate primary and general accounts through the Primary Final Report (03/01-03/03/2026), both counted; her general account showed no expenditures. On every report: itemized expenditures sum to line 24, lines 24+25+26 = line 27 = line 8 = line 20 (expenditures by category), beginning balance + loans + contributions - expenditures = closing balance, and each report's beginning balance equals the prior closing balance. Sanders' total equals her Pre-Election cumulative expenditures ($9,897,952.48) less the cumulative before 2025 ($1,801,216.49). Love's and Shelby's totals equal their filed cumulative expenditures. Love's October 2025 report appears twice in the state list (same figures) and is counted once. No loan repayments or returned contributions in any report.

Total disbursements (schedules 2A gross disbursements + 2B transfers out + 2C charitable donations) from the filed CF-2 cover pages, latest amendment of each report. Every schedule's itemized entries summed against its filed total, to the cent, for all reports (for amended reports, entries marked Removed excluded). Beginning balance plus contributions minus disbursements equals the Pre-Election ending balance for both campaigns, to the cent (Crowley $429.87 to $4,142,201.48; Tiffany $10,709.44 to $4,801,735.23), and each report's beginning balance equals the prior report's ending balance. The 2026 periods also sum to each Pre-Election cover's calendar year-to-date total. Crowley filed no report for Jan-Jun 2025 (committee exempt until 2025-09-12); his 2026 January Continuing report starts from the $429.87 balance carried since 2021 and its 2025 year-to-date equals the period, so no 2025 spending is missed. Tiffany's committee reported $0 spent Jan-Jun 2025 (filed as Citizens for Tiffany). In-kind contributions received (non-cash goods and services; 2026 year-to-date Tiffany $3,762,006.17, Crowley $429,019.43) are not cash disbursements and are not counted.

Spent is the sum of each report's filed cash expenditures (itemized + non-itemized) across all monthly, weekly and daily reports. Tuberville's $472,355.02 in line-of-credit expenditures is excluded because it does not pass through the cash balance; his $438,071.13 in repayments to Chain Bridge Bank are counted as regular expenditures. The state bulk transaction files (amended rows included) sum to each report's expenditure totals exactly for both committees; beginning balance + receipts - expenditures = ending balance on every report, and reports chain in filing order (gaps are covered by major contribution reports). Bulk receipt rows run $150,000 (Tuberville) and $500 (Jones, an amended 05/17/2026 daily report) short of the reported totals; this affects receipts only. Tuberville filed no weekly report for 10/24-10/30/2026; daily reports cover 10/26-10/30 and 11/02 and the balances still chain. Only his state governor committee is counted; his FEC committee is excluded.

Spent is Form B-1 line 14, cash expenditures, summed over the 2025 annual and the five 2026 statements (1st primary, 2nd primary, post primary, 1st general, 2nd general), latest amended version of each. Line 14 excludes in-kind contributions, matching how the other states are counted; line 16 total expenditures including in-kind is Pillen $12,809,697.42 and Walz $4,333,699.32. On every statement, cash on hand at beginning plus cash receipts minus cash expenditures equals cash on hand at close, to the cent; each statement's opening cash equals the prior close; previous expenditures plus this period's equals the election-year total (line 17). The 2026 line 16 sums equal line 17 on the 2nd general statements: Pillen $11,519,410.03, Walz $4,202,563.83. Itemized campaign expenses from the NADC bulk expenditure files, grouped by statement period, equal line 14 on every statement, and in-kind expenditures equal line 15, to the cent (third-party payee itemizations are separate and not added). Walz's committee (7640) was renamed from Lynne Walz for Legislature; its 2024 activity is excluded. Lindstrom for Nebraska (10530) registered in 2026 and has filed one statement, the 1st general (2026-01-01 to 2026-09-29): $49.50 cash spending plus $16,000 in-kind. No 2nd general statement from it was on file on 2026-11-04. His earlier committee, Friends of Lindstrom (7582), reported no 2025 activity and is not counted.

For every bank report counted, itemized bank-reported expenditures sum to the filed expenditure total to the cent, and start balance + credits - expenditures = end balance with each report's start balance equal to the prior end balance. Healey's filed bank expenditures through September total $7,694,386.69, which includes $1,383,445.59 moved to the committee's own money-market savings account ($383,445.59 on 2025-05-12, $1,000,000.00 on 2026-04-01; the savings balance rises by exactly those amounts); those transfers are excluded, giving $6,310,941.10. Her October report adds $3,306,376.57 (80 items summing to that to the cent; $3,292,308.31 + $614,272.76 credits - $3,306,376.57 = $600,204.50 end balance; savings unchanged at $83,442.28, so no transfer to savings), for $9,617,317.67. Contribution refunds (about $170K for Healey) stay in, as filed. James's October report adds $6,552.32 (8 items, to the cent). James's $248 out-of-pocket External Activity Report (2025-02-28 to 2025-03-01) is not counted. Merchant fees are netted from credits by the bank and are not in the expenditure totals. Minogue's spending is largely self-funded.

Spent is the sum of each report's filed cover-sheet total political expenditures (totalExpendAmount). Itemized expenditures (Schedules F1, F2, F4, G) plus the filed unitemized amount equal the cover-sheet total to the cent on every report counted, except Hinojosa's 30-day pre-primary report (2026-01-01 to 01-22), where itemized rows sum $1,314.78 below the filed total; the filed total is used. Investment purchases (Schedule F3) are not expenditures and are excluded. Abbott combines his candidate account (filer 00019652, $5,316,767.63) and his campaign committee Texans for Greg Abbott (filer 00051153, $182,295,029.84), minus $4,750,000 the committee transferred to the candidate account (2026-08-11 and 2026-09-23) so it is not counted twice. Balance check does not reconcile: the Texas cover sheet has no beginning-balance line, and rolling the prior report's 'contributions maintained' forward (plus contributions, minus in-kind, minus expenditures) matches the filed figure only for Dixon's last two reports and some of Abbott's candidate-account reports; Texans for Greg Abbott is off by $0.1M to $4.5M per report (it holds investments) and Hinojosa by $1K to $294K per report in both directions. Dixon has no report covering 2025-01-01 to 06-30 in the file; his July-December 2025 report shows no expenditures.

Spent is the Board's 'Expenses (F,Q,T,U)' total for 2025-01-01 to 2026-11-05 (office Governor, all statuses), net of expenditure refunds received (L): Hochul $33,764,390.89 less $92,042.80, Blakeman $20,993,306.05 less $4,837.00. Left out, as elsewhere: contributions refunded to donors (M: Hochul $4,949,123.68, Blakeman $47,724.77), in-kind (D: Hochul $120,747.17, Blakeman $1,000.00) and Blakeman's transfers out to other committees (H: $308,850.00). The Board's 'Monies Out' is exactly the sum of those parts for both. Balance check: Blakeman's committee registered 2025-12-10, so his monies in ($22,625,022.64) less monies out ($21,350,880.82) equals the current balance the Board shows ($1,274,141.82) to the cent; Hochul's all-time monies in ($115,514,841.72) less all-time monies out ($103,213,555.08) equals her current balance ($12,301,286.64) to the cent. Itemized check: Hochul's itemized F records dated from 2025 sum to $38,203,060.86, which includes $4,420,743.84 of credit card payments whose underlying charges are itemized separately; without them it is $33,782,317.02, within $17,926.13 (0.05%) of the Board's total. Blakeman's itemized F and T records sum to $21,021,181.22, within $27,875.17 (0.13%). The Board's own totals are used. The latest transactions for both are dated 2026-10-19. An earlier attempt read about $38.2M for Hochul from itemized records: that double-counted the credit card payments. The Board's per-committee totals page needs the search filters set first (Governor, 2025-01-01 to 2026-11-05) and shows zeros when opened directly, so both candidates link to the search page.

Spent is the filed campaign-to-date Total Monetary Expenditures (line G) on the Oct 20 CCDR summary page, latest version of each report. Per-report G values sum to it, and beginning balance plus contributions, loans and interest minus expenditures equals each report's ending balance, to the cent (Bottoms $0 to $668,563.71; Jackson $0 to $9,147,436.12). Itemized expenditures in the Commission's public transaction data summed per report match each report's Section 3 total (line 7) to the cent for all five Bottoms reports and two of four Jackson reports; for Jackson's Apr 30 and Jul 31 reports the transaction data's credit-card entries are $3,400.37 and $405.29 below the filed credit-card subtotals, while the filed subtotals add to line 7 exactly. Bottoms's Jul 31 report: summary-page expenditures ($2,703,807.16) are $0.95 below the detailed-summary line 11 because of a $0.95 returned unitemized expenditure; the summary-page figure reconciles the balance and is used. Bottoms's total includes $314,897.96 of loan repayments, which Georgia's form counts as monetary expenditures. In-kind contributions (non-cash) are not counted.

Summed cash disbursements (all 'campaign expenses'; no loan or payable repayments) from each CF-2 summary page, latest filed version. Total cash - ending balance = disbursements on every report and each report opens at the prior report's ending balance. The Board's itemized-expenditure search for 2025-01-01 to 2026-10-26 returns campaign-expenditure totals equal to the summed summaries to the cent for all three. Foulkes's $77,064.27 in returned contributions is netted from receipts on the filed form and is not counted; in-kind contributions are not counted. Block's committee reported no activity in 2025; his 2026 spending is partly self-funded (loans payable rose $220,250 in 2026).

Spent is the Division's expenditure total summed over each campaign's treasurer's reports; it includes reimbursements (the database's 'Other' column is that subset, not an addition) and is net of refunds received. For the four largest the itemized expenditure records sum to that total to the cent: Donalds 3,576 records, Jolly 3,437, Russo 147, Jewett 15. Excluded: Jewett's $23.20 dated 2024, and one Jolly petty-cash record of -$270 that the Division's total also leaves out. The four smallest are their filed totals, not checked against itemized records; Datto has filed nothing after March 31, 2026. Florida's database shows no cash balances, so no balance check was possible. In-kind contributions are not counted (Donalds $4,108,776.55, Jolly $660,569.65).

Spent is the sum of line 4c (Total Expenditures, Form C + C1) across all nine filed period reports for each committee; one-day 48-hour contribution reports filed after the Third General Report are not counted. Both committees opened at $0 on 2025-01-01, and every report's opening balance equals the prior report's closing balance. Opening plus contributions minus expenditures equals each report's closing balance and the final closing balance (Haaland $967,455.71, Hull $248,126.71) to the cent. Itemized Form C entries in each filed PDF sum to that report's 4c total to the cent for all 18 reports. The SOS bulk expenditure CSV does not match the filed PDFs: it is $89,362.36 short for Haaland and $1,589.00 over for Hull (both in a few reports); the filed reports are used.

Moore (Wes For Maryland): itemized monetary expenditures plus itemized reimbursement expenditures equal line 5 to the cent on all 5 reports; prior balance + contributions - line 9 = ending balance on every report; reports chain except Pre-Primary 1's prior balance is $63.60 below the amended 2026 Annual's ending balance, matching a $63.60 difference in cumulative expenditures carried from the pre-amendment Annual. Cox (Dan for Governor): 2026 Annual is an affidavit of under $1,000 in contributions and expenditures (no amounts reported), so his figure covers 01/15/2026-10/18/2026; itemized monetary expenditures equal line 5 on all 4 reports; balance identity (with loans) holds and reports chain. Ellis (Ellis/Andrews for Maryland, public financing committee): itemized sums equal line 5 on 4 reports; identity holds and reports chain; sum equals the filed total-to-date of $15,472.97; Pre-General 2 is an affidavit of under $1,000 with no amounts, so coverage ends 08/18/2026. Excluded: the Moore Miller For Maryland slate and a separate 'Ellis, Andy Campaign Donations for' committee (no office listed; 2026 reports show $28,311.98 in expenditures; no transfers to Ellis/Andrews found).

Spent is the sum of each report's Column A line 5, Total Expenditures, using the latest amendment of each report. For both committees line 5 equals line 16 (Schedule B expenditures made); there were no loan repayments or payments of unpaid bills after 2024. The sums match the Schedule B rows in the CSC's open-data expenditure set (hicscdata.hawaii.gov 3maa-4fgr, 2025-01-01 to 2026-10-19), to the cent: Green 751 items, $2,053,054.31; Cordery 733 items, $369,355.36. They also equal the 2nd preliminary general report's election-to-date line 16 minus pre-2025 spending ($874,539.48 Green, $3,623.92 Cordery). Each report's beginning cash + receipts - expenditures = ending cash, and each period opens at the prior period's close. Green amended his 2024-2026 reports on 2026-08-21 and his 1st preliminary general on 2026-10-05; the amended 1st preliminary general adds $1,175.22 of spending over the original.

Spent is the sum of each report's filed Summary Page line 6, payments made (cash, Schedule E total). Including unpaid bills and in-kind contributions (line 11, total expenditures made) would give Becerra $34,324,356.30 and Hilton $31,820,044.06. On every report, itemized Schedule E payments equal the filed itemized total to the cent, and beginning cash plus receipts plus miscellaneous increases minus payments equals the filed ending cash. Becerra's ending cash carries to the next report's beginning cash exactly. Hilton's does not: five of six beginning balances differ from the prior ending balance (+$1,090.00, -$27,527.53, +$4,904.72, +$72,415.08, -$22,172.89), and his last report's 2026 year-to-date payments are $40,763.71 above the sum of his 2026 period totals (Becerra: $110.50). No amendments filed. Late-contribution and independent-expenditure committees using the candidates' names are not included.

Summed Total Monetary Expenditures (line C) from each filed report PDF's summary page; each matches the report's campaign-to-date figure, beginning balance + contributions - expenditures = ending balance, and each report opens at the prior close. In-kind expenditures are not counted (Scott $58,381.04). Against the state's itemized expenditure data (disclosure plus mass-media items): Judd matches to the cent; Scott's itemized data is $38,600 higher (a $39,000 TV buy deleted in his amended Oct 15 report still appears in mass-media data, and a $400 item on his Sep 1 report has no itemized record); Janoo's is $20,515.70 higher, exactly one set of three radio buys ($5,400 + $7,499.70 + $7,616) that appears on both 10/16 and 10/19 mass-media reports but once in her Oct 30 report. Filed totals are used. Janoo's figure is after a $2,000 refunded expenditure. The state's profile summary shows Scott's ending balance as $146,980.59; his filed Oct 30 report shows $134,800.59.
